references.text: Moses explains that the people come to him to seek God's will, and he brings their cases before God. This shows the same practice as in Num 27:5.
Jethro advises Moses to bring difficult cases before God, which establishes the principle Moses follows here.
Another case where Moses waited for the Lord's decision in a legal matter that required divine guidance.
Moses asked the people to wait while he sought the Lord's will regarding the Passover celebration for those who were unclean. The same pattern of bringing difficult cases before the Lord.
The case of the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath was brought before the Lord because it was unclear what should be done. A parallel situation to the daughters of Zelophehad.
Moses conveys the Lord's answer in the follow-up case concerning the inheritance and marriage of Zelophehad's daughters, which directly continues from this text.
